content:
# Tobit Chapter 3 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Disagreement 1 — TOB 3:2: Opening Doxology — "All Your Ways"

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "all your works and all your ways [are] mercy and truth and true judgment you-judge for-the-age" |
| LOGOS | "all your works are mercy and truth; you judge with true judgment forever" |
| PNEUMA | "Everything you do flows from mercy and faithfulness. Your judgments are true and just, now and always" |

**Issue:** The Greek has both pasai hai ergai (all your works) and pasai hai hodoi sou (all your ways). LOGOS inadvertently omits "all your ways." PNEUMA renders alētheia as "faithfulness" (which belongs to pistis/hesed) rather than "truth."

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "all your works and all your ways are mercy and truth; you judge with true judgment forever." Restores the omitted phrase from EMET; uses LOGOS structure.

---

## Disagreement 2 — TOB 3:3: Taxonomy of Sin

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "my sins and my ignorances and [those of] my fathers" |
| LOGOS | "my sins and the sins of my forefathers committed in ignorance" |
| PNEUMA | "my sins — or for the sins of my ancestors, who stumbled before you without fully knowing what they were doing" |

**Issue:** The Greek has three distinct elements: (1) my sins, (2) my agnoiai (ignorance-sins), (3) my fathers' sins. LOGOS collapses elements 2 and 3 by making "ignorance" modify the fathers' sins only. PNEUMA's "stumbled" is too mild for deliberate transgression.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "do not punish me for my sins and for my forefathers' sins committed in ignorance before you." SOPHIA follows LOGOS's natural English flow while acknowledging that agnoiai most naturally qualifies the ancestral sins in context.

---

## Disagreement 3 — TOB 3:4: "Proverb of Reproach"

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "a proverb of-reproach for all-the nations" |
| LOGOS | "a proverb of reproach among all the nations" |
| PNEUMA | "a cautionary tale, a byword of shame among every nation" |

**Issue:** Parabolēn oneidismou is a technical biblical phrase echoing Deut 28:37. The double rendering in PNEUMA ("cautionary tale, a byword") is an expansion.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "a proverb of reproach among all the nations where we have been scattered" (LOGOS). The formal idiom preserved; LOGOS's "among" is preferable to EMET's "for."

---

## Disagreement 4 — TOB 3:6: "Return to Dust/Earth"

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "that I may be released and may become earth" |
| LOGOS | "so that I may be released and return to dust" |
| PNEUMA | "Let me go. Let me turn back to dust" |

**Issue:** The Greek apallagō kai genōmai gē ("that I be released and become earth") is a death-wish expressed through the Genesis 3:19 topos. LOGOS's "return to dust" renders this allusion idiomatically. EMET's "become earth" is awkward.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Return to the earth" (slightly over "dust" to match the Greek gē more exactly, while the allusion to Gen 3:19 is still clear).

---

## Disagreement 5 — TOB 3:6: Structure of the Death Petition (Double Request)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Preserves both verbatim with the Greek phrase structure |
| LOGOS | Preserves both with natural English variation |
| PNEUMA | Varies significantly: "It is better to die than to live like this" and "It is better to die than to live this way — scorned, broken, with no relief in sight" |

**Issue:** PNEUMA's second occurrence adds "scorned, broken, with no relief in sight" — three qualifiers not in the Greek. The Greek second occurrence reads: "kreitton gar moi apothanein ē zēn, hoti oneidismous pseudeis ēkousa" = "for it is better for me to die than to live, because false reproaches I have heard."

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** Both occurrences preserved. PNEUMA's additions to the second occurrence are removed. SOPHIA follows LOGOS: "For it is better for me to die than to endure such great distress in my life and to hear such reproach."

---

## Disagreement 6 — TOB 3:8: Asmodeus's Full Designation

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "Asmodeus the-evil demon" |
| LOGOS | "the evil demon Asmodeus" |
| PNEUMA | "the demon Asmodeus" |

**Issue:** The Greek Asmodaios ho daimonion to ponēron — "Asmodeus, the evil demon" — is his full title throughout the book. PNEUMA omits "evil" (ponēron) without textual basis.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "the evil demon Asmodeus" (LOGOS). The descriptor "evil" is part of the text's way of identifying this entity and must be preserved throughout.

---

## Disagreement 7 — TOB 3:9: The Servant's Curse

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "Let there not be seen from you son or daughter for the age" |
| LOGOS | "Let there never be seen from you son or daughter to the end of the age" |
| PNEUMA | "Don't you dare have children who have to live with what you are!" |

**Issue:** The Greek mē ophtheiē sou huios ē thugater eis ton aiōna is a formal imprecatory curse, wishing permanent childlessness. PNEUMA's rendering turns it into a contemporary insult and invents a reason for the curse not in the text.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "May there never be seen from you son or daughter forever!" (modified LOGOS). The formal curse register is essential; the exclamation mark captures the viciousness of delivery.

---

## Disagreement 8 — TOB 3:10: Sarah's Decision

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "It is better for me not to hang myself but to pray to the Lord that I may die and may hear no longer reproaches in my life" |
| LOGOS | "It is better for me not to hang myself, but to pray to the Lord that I may die and hear these reproaches no more in my life" |
| PNEUMA | "No. I won't hang myself. I will pray. I will ask God to let me die — and then at least I'll never have to hear these words again" |

**Issue:** PNEUMA's fragmentary sentences are dramatic but sacrifice the formal deliberative structure of the Greek. The Greek conditional reasoning (suicide → shame → alternative) should read as a logical self-argument.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. The full deliberative sentence structure is preserved: "It is better for me not to hang myself, but to pray to the Lord that I may die and hear these reproaches no more in my life."

---

## Disagreement 9 — TOB 3:14-15: Sarah's Defense — Purity and Kinship

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "I am pure from all sin of a-man…I am the only-begotten of my father" |
| LOGOS | "I am pure from every sin with a man…I am my father's only child" |
| PNEUMA | "I am innocent. I have never been with a man…I am all he has — his only child" |

**Issue (v.14):** The Greek katharē apo pasēs hamartias andros carries both ritual and sexual purity before God — the legal-ritual register should not be flattened to "innocent" (PNEUMA).

**Issue (v.15):** "Only-begotten" (monogenēs) is accurate (EMET) but has been so thoroughly appropriated by NT Christology that it creates an unintended theological resonance in this context. "Only child" (LOGOS) is cleaner.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** Verse 14: "I am pure from every sin with a man" (LOGOS). Verse 15: "I am my father's only child" (LOGOS).

---

## Disagreement 10 — TOB 3:16: God's Title at the Hearing

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "before the glory of God the Great" |
| LOGOS | "before the glory of the great God" |
| PNEUMA | "before the throne of the great and glorious God" |

**Issue:** The Greek enōpion tēs doxēs tou megalou theou = "before the glory of the great God." PNEUMA introduces "throne" (not in the text) and reverses the adjective/noun structure.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "before the glory of the great God" (LOGOS). Exact rendering of the Greek.

---

## Disagreement 11 — TOB 3:17: The Binding of Asmodeus

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "to bind Asmodeus the evil demon" |
| LOGOS | "to bind the evil demon Asmodeus" |
| PNEUMA | "freeing her from the shadow of Asmodeus" |

**Issue:** The Greek dēsai ton Asmodaion to daimonion to ponēron = "to bind Asmodeus the evil demon." This is an angelic binding action — a formal supernatural restraint. PNEUMA's "freeing her from the shadow of" is a loose paraphrase that loses the specific imagery of demonic binding.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "to bind the evil demon Asmodeus" (LOGOS). The binding action is theologically precise and must be preserved.

---

## Disagreement 12 — TOB 3:17: The Lot-Casting and Inheritance

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "because it fell-by-lot to Tobias to-inherit her before all-the-others who were-desiring to-take-her" |
| LOGOS | "For it had fallen by lot to Tobias to inherit her before all the other men who had wished to take her" |
| PNEUMA | "It had been ordained from on high that Tobias was the one she was meant for — he had always had the prior claim" |

**Issue:** The Greek eklērothe autē Tōbias pro pantōn tōn thelontōn labein autēn uses the lot-casting verb (klēroō) and the inheritance-marriage legal framework. PNEUMA loses both the lot mechanism and the legal terminology.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "It had fallen by lot to Tobias to inherit her" preserves both the lot-casting and the inheritance-law framing essential to the story's legal logic.

---

**Total disagreements logged: 12**
